description: TZ jsonrpc.rs (928) + stdio.rs (484), FZ mcp_protocol/ (stdio 276 + http 377), GZ cli/mcp.rs (1258) each hand-roll JSON-RPC framing, initialize handshake, tools/list plumbing, error envelopes, stdio loop. MCP spec compliance is drift-forbidden — protocol layer belongs in one crate; engines supply a tool registry + dispatch closure. Also carries the FZ HTTP transport so any engine can opt in. Per-engine tool schemas stay engine-owned (decided).
title: wave 3: zero-mcp — shared JSON-RPC 2.0 + MCP stdio server core

description: GZ plans 1TP adoption (graphzero-0odn: symbol ordinals, gauge, TA registry) and FZ may follow. TZ owns one-token-atoms fixtures, gauge arithmetic, tz://o/<gen>/<ord> ordinal grammar today. If 2+ engines speak 1TP it is a shared protocol: fixtures, atom certification checker, ordinal grammar + allocation arithmetic move to zero-gauge — also the right place to fix the omega-math finding that standalone digit atoms do not certify composed refs (certify complete grammar instances in context, per provider). Trigger: when graphzero-0odn is scheduled. Do NOT extract before then.
title: conditional wave 5: 1TP atoms/gauge/ordinal grammar as zero-gauge

description: (A) Capability peer validation: FZ core/capability.rs DescriptorFields tolerant extractor, GZ zeroref_capability.rs validate_peer_descriptor, TZ mcp/capability_descriptor.rs — each engine parses the OTHER engines descriptors with alias tolerance (hash.algo vs hash.algorithm, layout_version key drift). This code exists only to reconcile drift; sharing the descriptor schema + validator removes the reason it exists. Engines keep engine-owned fields (remediation, limits). Per-dimension clamp policy vocabulary ({byte,line_start,line_end}, cf. FZ b369c99) becomes the shared type. (B) zero-telemetry: prevented_* counter schema GZ writes into the TZ session ledger (graphzero-ay7m) is cross-engine wire format — types + canonical serialization shared, sinks engine-owned.
title: wave 4: capability negotiation + cross-engine telemetry schema into shared crates

comments.text: DECISION (user): start with three separate binaries (tokenzero, fszero, graphzero) as three commands — matches the use-one-alone model and is simplest. Busybox-style single zero multiplexer binary deferred; revisit only if there is real demand.

description: Ship story for 1..3 engines + shared substrate. Facts: engines are statically linked single binaries; zerostack crates are compile-time git deps baked in at build — users never install zerostack; only builds fetch it (cargo via SHA pin). Deliverables: (1) GitHub Releases per engine (macos-arm64/x86_64, linux-x86_64/arm64, windows-x86_64) via CI matrix. (2) homebrew tap AdityaVG13/homebrew-zerostack (already referenced in GZ README): formulas tokenzero/fszero/graphzero + meta formula zerostack installing all three. (3) installer script hosted in THIS repo: curl | sh with --all or per-engine flags (winget/scoop manifests later). (4) docs/store-layout.md: canonical .zerostack/ on-disk contract — per-repo store, engine namespaces (fszero/repos/<sid>, graphzero/projects/<key>, tokenzero), shared CAS blobs unified by pinned layout version; installing engines in any order adds namespaces beside existing ones, no migration; version skew across engines guarded by capability negotiation (worst case read_only/disabled, never corruption). (5) later: publish zero-* to crates.io so cargo install tokenzero works without git — blocked on stable semver; keep SHA pins until then.
title: distribution: prebuilt binaries, homebrew tap, unified installer, .zerostack layout doc

wave 1.5: CAS publish/GC core + .zerostack store-root resolution into zero-store
description: Two drift-forbidden pieces move into zero-store. (A) CAS internals: TZ shared_cas.rs (1,485 LOC incl. zerostack.cas-gc.v1 GC), FZ core/cas.rs (341), GZ store CAS — shared publish protocol (temp+fsync+rename), object verify, and the GC state machine live once; fixes the omega-math CRITICAL TOCTOU (GC unlinking concurrently republished objects; publish never takes the GC lock) exactly once instead of three times. (B) Store-root resolution: TZ engine/workspace.rs (~250), FZ core/zerostack_store.rs (137), GZ store/zerostack_store.rs (533) all reimplement .zerostack/ detection, ZEROSTACK_STORE_ROOT/ZERO_STACK_STORE_ROOT precedence, shared-store opt-in, and sha256 project-key namespacing — if these drift, engines put data in different places and interop silently breaks. Shared module owns layout + resolution; engines keep alias envs (TOKENZERO_SHARED_STORE etc.) as thin wrappers. TZ = PR, GZ/FZ direct. Equality gates: digest byte-identical per engine + store-path golden tests (same inputs resolve same paths before/after).

Largest remaining pool: TZ mcp/codemode/* (~8K: exec 3803, journal 969, containment 803, store 702, parser 462), FZ codemode/* (~2.5K: js 732, host 603, connector 466), GZ codemode/* (~3.5K: quickjs 638, steps 574, executor 517, response 512, host_permit 495). Shared crate owns: rquickjs engine setup (unify TZ 0.10 -> 0.12 to match FZ), sandbox/containment policy, plan parsing, step journaling, host-permit model, response envelopes. Engines register only their own host functions/connectors (zero.token.*, zero.fs.*, zero.graph.*). Bisectable: rquickjs bump lands as its own commit inside the wave.
title: wave 2: zero-codemode — shared rquickjs runtime, containment, plan/step machinery
wave 1.4: move zerostack-machine-permit into hub crates (unblocks two engine p0s)
description:
zerostack-machine-permit is cross-engine shared infrastructure that currently lives inside TokenZero at TokenZero/crates/zerostack-machine-permit. Both other engines already depend on it from outside TokenZero, so the hub is its correct home.

Current consumers:
- FSZero/Cargo.toml:87  zerostack-machine-permit = { path = "../tokenzero/crates/zerostack-machine-permit" }
- GraphZero/crates/graphzero-query/Cargo.toml:28  git dep on the tokenzero repo, rev 45e242cb63ede0dedd8e10e3f8f322fe8d360c20

BUG found while surveying: the FSZero path dep spells the sibling directory "tokenzero" but the real directory is "TokenZero". It resolves only because macOS APFS is case-insensitive. On a case-sensitive filesystem (Linux CI, most containers) FSZero fails to build. Confirmed: /Users/aditya/AI/tokenzero and /Users/aditya/AI/TokenZero both stat successfully on this machine, and only TokenZero is the real entry.

Also cross-repo: GraphZero/crates/graphzero-test-support/Cargo.toml:23 path-deps ../../../TokenZero/crates/tokenzero-recovery, which is the other half of the graphzero-ml4r standalone-build failure.

Deliverables:
1. Move the crate to ZeroStack/crates/zerostack-machine-permit, add to the hub workspace members.
2. Repoint FSZero and GraphZero to the hub via pinned git rev, matching how zero-abi and zero-ref are already pinned.
3. Remove the TokenZero copy, or leave a re-export shim for one release if TokenZero-internal callers need it.
4. Verify FSZero builds with a case-sensitive path check, not just on macOS.

Unblocks: fszero-ixka (p0 standalone build), graphzero-ml4r (p0 standalone build).
Related: zerostack-hxl deliverable 5 (crates.io publish removes the git pin entirely).

comments.author: aditya
comments.text:
Progress, hub side landed and verified.

Done:
- crates/zerostack-machine-permit added to the hub, src copied byte-identical from TokenZero (diff -r clean, marker SRC_BYTE_IDENTICAL).
- Manifest rewritten to hub convention: explicit version 0.1.0, edition.workspace, license.workspace, explicit description. TokenZero had inherited version/repository/homepage/readme/keywords/categories/rust-version from its own workspace, which the hub workspace does not define.
- Added to hub workspace members.
- Equality gate: 22/22 inline tests pass in the hub under edition 2021 stable, matching 22/22 in TokenZero under edition 2024 nightly. The crate is edition-agnostic. Hub suite went 38 to 60 tests.

- FSZero repointed and verified. The case-sensitivity build break is fixed:
    - was: zerostack-machine-permit = { path = "../tokenzero/crates/zerostack-machine-permit" }
    - now: zerostack-machine-permit = { path = "../ZeroStack/crates/zerostack-machine-permit" }
  This both fixes the Linux/case-sensitive-filesystem failure and removes the FSZero to TokenZero coupling. Verified: cargo metadata exit 0, cargo check -p zerostack-machine-permit compiles v0.1.0 from the hub path, Cargo.lock updated 1.4.0 to 0.1.0.

Deliberately not done, and why:
- GraphZero left untouched. It already uses a git dep on the tokenzero repo rev 45e242cb63ede0dedd8e10e3f8f322fe8d360c20, which is push-independent and works today. Converting it to a path dep would introduce a sibling-checkout requirement and make graphzero-ml4r worse. It should flip straight to a hub git dep.
- TokenZero copy left in place. Removing it entangles this work with open PR #31 on branch adopt-zero-ref.

Blocked on a push, not on code: FSZero and GraphZero can only take pinned git deps on the hub once this hub commit exists on the zerostack remote, the same way zero-abi and zero-ref are pinned at 90cdbfad5fa5bc5d601e841def2416d64810a487. No push authority in this session, so the flip is the remaining step.

Open risk while the flip is pending: two byte-identical copies of the crate exist, hub and TokenZero, with no guard against divergence. Worth a hub check that compares them, or just land the TokenZero removal promptly.

Note the version goes backwards for anyone who was reading it, 1.4.0 in TokenZero to 0.1.0 in the hub, because the hub versions its foundation crates at 0.1.0. Harmless for path and rev-pinned git deps, but it needs a decision before any crates.io publish (zerostack-hxl deliverable 5).

comments.author: aditya
comments.text:
Pushed. Hub rev d8903ed958867670ad1bd669e06e4c31e72b2c29 is on origin/main.

Landed:
- ZeroStack: two commits, bd4fbaf (retire bd for br, remove bd git hooks, document zero.* routing) and d8903ed (extract the crate). Pushed e3ef302..d8903ed.
- TokenZero: PR #31 merged as e65e4c3, plus 048841b carrying the br-format beads export. Local main synced to origin.
- FSZero: 4646af0, flipped to the pinned hub git dep. Verified cargo check resolves v0.1.0 from git+.../zerostack?rev=d8903ed and Cargo.lock records that source. Pushed 69cf154..4646af0. The case-sensitivity build break is gone, so a clean clone on Linux now works.

Remaining, both deliberate:
1. GraphZero not repointed. That checkout has 76 modified tracked files and 11 untracked, including a live refactor across crates/graphzero-cli. Editing its Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock would entangle this work with an in-flight session and risk pushing half-finished state. Sent Agent Mail message id 509 to AzurePelican and PurpleRiver in the GraphZero project with the exact one-line change for crates/graphzero-query/Cargo.toml:28.
2. TokenZero copy of the crate still present, so two byte-identical copies exist with no divergence guard. Removing it is deliverable 3 and is now unblocked, since the hub rev is published.

Also removed as part of retiring bd: core.hooksPath pointed at .beads/hooks and pre-push ran bd hooks run pre-push, which would have written to the retired Dolt store on every push and re-created the divergence this session just fixed. Incidentally dogfooded the extracted crate under real contention: a zero_execute call failed with machine_permit_busy on /tmp/zerostack-codemode-heavy-8a6d3b8d1b260a41.permit held by another live session, and succeeded on retry. Correct behavior, and it confirms multiple sessions are sharing the permit as designed.

title: zero-store adoption: no engine consumes it yet, three local CAS copies still live
description:
Gap found while surveying all three engines. The hub shipped crates/zero-store, but every engine pins only zero-abi and zero-ref at rev 90cdbfad5fa5bc5d601e841def2416d64810a487. Nothing depends on zero-store, so the extraction has produced no deduplication yet.

Verified local CAS/store code still owned per engine:
- TokenZero: crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/shared_cas.rs (1485 LOC, includes the zerostack.cas-gc.v1 GC), embedded_store.rs, segment_store.rs, crates/tokenzero-mcp/src/codemode/store.rs, crates/tokenzero/src/zerostack_store.rs
- FSZero: src/core/cas.rs (341 LOC), src/core/zerostack_store.rs, src/core/embedded_store.rs, src/core/cdc.rs, src/core/ref_resolver.rs, src/core/recovery/*
- GraphZero: crates/graphzero-store/src/store/blob_store.rs, store/ref_index.rs, store/fs_replace.rs, blob_put path in store/indexer.rs:2310-2407

FSZero has no bead of its own for this at all. TokenZero tracks it only indirectly via tokenzero-9d2x, which names "Wave 1.5 zero-store cutover" as its fix vehicle. GraphZero tracks fragments via store-schema-version-93rn and zeroref-v1-shared-cas-1ghi.

This bead owns the engine-side adoption sequencing that zerostack-sce (the code move) does not cover. Blocked on zerostack-sce landing GC plus store-root resolution, because adopting today would mean adopting a strictly weaker store.

Equality gate per engine: digests byte-identical before and after, and store-path golden tests proving the same inputs resolve to the same paths.

title: declare canonical zero-ref line-clamp policy per dimension (two engine p1s wait on this)
description:
crates/zero-ref already implements the mechanism: LineEndPolicy::Strict and LineEndPolicy::ClampEnd, with select_fragment defaulting to Strict (crates/zero-ref/src/lib.rs, select_fragment at ~line 345, policy match at ~line 410).

What is missing is the contract decision about which policy is canonical for which dimension, and whether the capability descriptor must advertise it. Without that, engines diverge by default:
- TokenZero clamps (tokenzero-52gv, p1)
- shared strict selection errors with RangeOutOfBounds
- FSZero calls select_fragment_with_policy explicitly at src/core/zeroref.rs:40 (fszero-00vq, p1)

So the same ref over a short file can succeed in one engine and error in another, which is exactly the drift the shared crate exists to prevent.

Today the only hub-side mention is inside zerostack-b3l, a p2 wave-4 bead covering the per-dimension clamp policy vocabulary ({byte, line_start, line_end}, cf. FSZero b369c99). That is a priority inversion: two p1 engine beads are blocked on a p2 hub decision. This bead pulls the decision out of b3l so it can land independently of the capability-negotiation work.

Deliverables:
1. Decide and document canonical policy per dimension in the hub contract.
2. Encode it in zero-ref as the default, so engines cannot silently pick differently.
3. Extend the golden-vector fixture with clamp and strict cases at the boundary.
4. State whether the capability descriptor must advertise the policy, and if so add it to the conformance schema.

Unblocks: tokenzero-52gv, fszero-00vq.
notes: Implemented canonical v1 bounds policy: byte strict, line_start strict, line_end clamp. zero-ref defaults now encode ClampEnd; explicit strict APIs remain for validation. Fixture v2 includes canonical clamp and strict override boundary vectors. docs/zeroref.md states policy is fixed by ZeroRef v1 and not separately capability-negotiated. Verified on spark-1672 via rch: zero-ref 4/4 tests passed; clippy -D warnings passed; rustfmt and git diff --check passed. Independent review's versioning wording concern was fixed by clarifying this establishes the previously unspecified v1 default.
close_reason: Canonical ZeroRef bounds policy implemented and documented. Golden fixture v2 covers clamp and strict boundaries. Remote Spark tests and clippy pass.

title: GraphZero has a second canonical-JSON implementation off zero-abi
description:
Undetected drift, no bead in any repo before this one.

GraphZero/crates/graphzero-pack/src/manifest.rs:85 defines its own unsigned_canonical_json. GraphZero already re-exports zero_abi canonical JSON elsewhere (crates/graphzero-query/src/operation_abi/schema.rs re-exports zero_abi canonical_json, canonical_schema_json, normalize_schema, schema_diff, and digest.rs:53,58 call zero_abi contract_digest*), so this one function is a parallel implementation of the single most drift-forbidden primitive in the stack.

Canonical JSON feeds the contract digest. If the pack manifest hashes bytes that zero-abi would encode differently, pack manifests and contract digests disagree about identity, and the disagreement is silent because both sides produce valid-looking hashes.

Deliverables:
1. Confirm whether unsigned_canonical_json is byte-identical to zero_abi canonical_json today. Differential test over the zero-abi fixture corpus plus pack manifest fixtures.
2. If identical, delete it and call zero-abi.
3. If not identical, that is a live digest bug: record which manifests were hashed with the divergent encoder before replacing it.
4. Add a hub-side guard so a second canonical-JSON implementation cannot reappear unnoticed.

Related: tokenzero-hks0 (canonical-JSON digest hardening against zero-abi), tokenzero-ghv7 (contract digest depends on registry declaration order).

title: conformance suite is stale and unwired: all reports predate three weeks of engine work
description:
The hub owns conformance/ but nothing keeps it current.

Every artifact in conformance/reports is dated 2026-07-01: fz-*, gz-*, tz-* (23 files). Three weeks of engine changes have landed since, including zero-abi and zero-ref adoption in all three engines. The suite is not run by any CI workflow in this repo.

Meanwhile the engine side reports a contradiction worth resolving here: GraphZero closed zeroref-v1-shared-cas-1ghi.8 and 1ghi.9 as done, while their own notes say external blockers were unresolved and the conformance gate deliberately stays BLOCKED with docs/contracts/zeroref-conformance-evidence.json in status pending. So the hub currently has no independent evidence that the engines conform, and the engine tracker records a closed-but-unproven state.

Deliverables:
1. Re-run the conformance suite against current engine HEADs, one report per engine, committed.
2. Wire it into hub CI so a stale suite fails rather than silently rots.
3. Record the report freshness contract: which engine revs each report attests to.
4. Reconcile the GraphZero pending-evidence contradiction, either by producing passing evidence or by reopening the closed beads.

Note: hub workspace is edition 2021 while all three engines are edition 2024 on nightly, so the suite must keep compiling under both.

title: retire legacy .beads/embeddeddolt in all four repos after the br migration
description:
Follow-up from the completed bd to br tracker migration.

All four repos now use br with SQLite at .beads/beads.db, and .beads/issues.jsonl is the br-written export. The old bd Dolt data still sits in .beads/embeddeddolt in every repo and is now a divergence trap: anyone who runs bd writes a second store that br cannot import, because bd emits comments[].id as a string where br requires an integer.

Migration outcome for the record, br is authoritative and no br content was overwritten:
- TokenZero 324 issues total, 19 recovered from Dolt that br had never seen
- FSZero 366 total, 12 recovered
- GraphZero 843 total, 8 recovered
- ZeroStack 7 total, SQLite bootstrapped from scratch, 1 UUIDv7 comment id normalized

Pre-migration backups are at /tmp/beads-backup-premigrate-20260725-<repo>. Those are temp-dir copies and will not survive a reboot.

Deliverables:
1. Move the backups somewhere durable, or confirm they are disposable.
2. Delete .beads/embeddeddolt in all four repos.
3. Confirm no CI job, git hook, or agent doc still invokes bd.
